name: Repo Blueprint
interact_justification: The README explains how to start a repository from the blueprint, what it gets and how updates work: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint#readme (German: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/README.de.md). Issues and pull requests are open on GitHub.
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states what an acceptable contribution needs: tests for new functionality and for every fix, the passing checks of scripts/check.sh, the coding standards of each language, a DCO sign-off on every commit, a Conventional Commit title and an entry under Unreleased in the changelog for every change for users. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#requirements-for-changes
floss_license_justification: The MIT-0 license (MIT No Attribution) is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
floss_license_osi_justification: The MIT-0 license (MIT No Attribution) is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
documentation_interface_justification: The README documents the questions of the template, the files and workflows a repository gets, the settings as code of blueprint.py and the updates: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint#readme
repo_public_justification: Repository on GitHub, which provides public git repositories with URLs.
repo_track_justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git can track the changes, who made them, and when they were made.
repo_interim_justification: Interim changes are visible in pull requests and on main between releases: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/commits/main
repo_distributed_justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git is distributed.
version_unique_justification: Every release has a unique version in version.txt and the release manifest and a matching tag; scripts/check.sh checks that they agree, and Copier copies and updates repositories from these tags: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/releases
version_semver_justification: Releases use Semantic Versioning, made by release-please from Conventional Commit titles: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/releases
release_notes_justification: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md and the GitHub releases, written by release-please from the merged pull requests.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerability (with a CVE) has been fixed in a release so far.
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues, with issue forms for bugs and feature requests: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/issues
report_responses_justification: No bug reports were submitted during the last 2-12 months; the project is newer than two months.
enhancement_responses_justification: No enhancement requests were submitted during the last 2-12 months; the project is newer than two months.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability report has been received during the last six months.
build_justification: The blueprint is a Copier template with a Python script of the standard library; no build step is required.
test_justification: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/tree/main/tests - pytest suite with 100 % branch coverage of blueprint.py against a simulated GitHub, and tests that render every kind of project; the Variants workflow runs the checks of every rendered project with its real tools.
test_invocation_justification: The tests run with bash scripts/check.sh or the standard pytest command: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#checks
test_most_justification: The suite covers every line and branch of blueprint.py and renders all nine kinds of projects, the licenses and the blueprint's own files, and checks their workflows, versions, locks and labels.
tests_are_added_justification: Changes are merged with tests, e.g. the fuzzing of the projects: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/pull/3
tests_documented_added_justification: The instructions for change proposals in CONTRIBUTING.md require tests for new functionality, and the checklist of the pull request template asks for them. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
warnings_justification: Ruff, mypy in strict mode, actionlint, ShellCheck, REUSE and CodeQL run in CI.
warnings_fixed_justification: CI fails on any Ruff, mypy, actionlint or REUSE finding; pull requests cannot merge until it is fixed.
warnings_strict_justification: mypy runs in strict mode, Ruff with the rule sets E, F, W, I, B, UP, SIM, PT and RUF, and pytest with --strict-markers, --strict-config and every warning as an error.
know_secure_design_justification: Secure design: every action pinned to a commit hash, read-only tokens by default, secrets only in environments that main alone may use, immutable releases with SBOM and signed provenance, and blueprint.py never reads or prints secret values.
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainer knows common vulnerability classes, including template and script injection in workflows; CodeQL, actionlint, Gitleaks, dependency review and fuzzing check for them.
crypto_published_justification: The blueprint implements and uses no cryptography of its own; it calls the GitHub CLI, which uses HTTPS.
crypto_call_justification: The blueprint uses no cryptography of its own.
crypto_floss_justification: The blueprint uses no cryptography of its own.
crypto_keylength_justification: The blueprint uses no cryptography of its own.
crypto_working_justification: The blueprint uses no cryptography of its own.
crypto_pfs_justification: The blueprint implements no key agreement protocol.
crypto_random_justification: The blueprint generates no cryptographic keys or nonces.
delivery_mitm_justification: The blueprint is distributed through GitHub over HTTPS; Copier copies it from release tags over HTTPS.
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hashes are retrieved over HTTP.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: There are no unpatched vulnerabilities of medium or higher severity; Dependabot and dependency review monitor dependencies.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: Critical vulnerabilities are fixed as soon as they are confirmed.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (Python and Actions), Ruff and mypy run on every push and pull request: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL with its security-extended queries analyzes the Python and the workflows on every pull request and every push to main; zizmor audits the workflows for their known attack patterns.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Medium and higher severity findings are fixed before merge.
static_analysis_often_justification: Static analysis runs on every push and pull request, and CodeQL also weekly.
dynamic_analysis_justification: Coverage-guided fuzzing with Atheris of how blueprint.py reads the answers of GitHub runs on every change and weekly: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/fuzz/fuzz_blueprint.py
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The project has no code in a memory-unsafe language: Python, Jinja templates, shell scripts and YAML.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Tests run with pytest assertions enabled.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No issue has been found so far; a finding fails the Fuzzing workflow, and the change cannot merge until it is fixed.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: The blueprint implements no security mechanism with its own cryptography; releases are signed by Sigstore and GitHub with SHA-256 digests.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions run pytest with a 100 % coverage gate, Ruff, mypy, actionlint, REUSE and the checks of all nine rendered kinds of projects on every push and pull request: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/actions
discussion_justification: GitHub supports discussions on issues and pull requests.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credentials are stored in the repository; Gitleaks scans every push and pull request: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/.github/workflows/secret-scan.yml
english_justification: Documentation, code and issue handling are in English.
hardening_justification: Every workflow starts without permissions, pins every action by commit hash (a setting of the repository), checks out without persisting credentials, runs under Harden-Runner, and keeps secrets in environments that only main can use.
crypto_used_network_justification: Every connection goes to GitHub through the GitHub CLI over HTTPS.
crypto_tls12_justification: The GitHub CLI uses TLS 1.2 or later, as GitHub requires.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: The GitHub CLI verifies TLS certificates by default, and the blueprint never turns that off.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: TLS certificates are verified in the handshake, before any HTTP header with a token is sent; TLS comes from the GitHub CLI and Python's standard library, which verify certificates by default, and the signatures of releases from Sigstore.
hardened_site_justification: GitHub Pages serves the project's website. It sends Strict-Transport-Security, but a project can't set Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options or X-Frame-Options there, so the website lacks them. The repository and its release downloads are on github.com, which sends its own hardening headers.
installation_common_justification: A repository installs the blueprint with copier copy gh:Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint, the common way of Copier templates, and stays current with copier update; a repository leaves it by deleting .copier-answers.yml and the workflow blueprint-update.yml.
dco_justification: Every commit carries a Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off (git commit -s); CONTRIBUTING.md requires it and links to https://developercertificate.org/. The required check dco of the Lint workflow fails a pull request with a commit without sign-off, and the repository requires a sign-off for web commits too. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#requirements-for-changes
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md documents the governance model: one maintainer with final responsibility for releases, repository access, security responses and direction; decisions are discussed in public issues and pull requests; every change reaches main through a pull request that passes all required checks; bots do the routine work with the least permissions. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
code_of_conduct_justification: The project follows a code of conduct in the spirit of the Contributor Covenant 2.1, in the standard location CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, with private reporting to the maintainer. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
roles_responsibilities_justification: GOVERNANCE.md defines the roles maintainer, contributor, reporter and bots with their responsibilities and the tasks they must perform; the table of maintainers says who has which role and which access. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities
access_continuity_justification: The maintainer has designated a successor through GitHub's account successor setting. Should the maintainer die, the successor can, once GitHub has confirmed it, transfer the repository to their own account or to an organization and carry it on there with administrator access: create and close issues, accept pull requests and publish releases. Everything needed to continue is in the repository (code, tests, workflows, settings as code, documentation), and the bots keep the dependencies current. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
bus_factor_justification: The bus factor is 2: the maintainer and the successor designated through GitHub's account successor setting, who can take over the repository. The documentation of the architecture, the security design, the decisions and the development, the tests with full coverage and the bots let the successor carry the project on. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
documentation_roadmap_justification: docs/roadmap.md describes what the blueprint intends to do in the next twelve months, until October 2027, and what it will not do. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md
documentation_architecture_justification: The README explains the high-level design: copier.yml with the questions, template/ with the files whose names carry their conditions, the workflows of this repository as the templates of every repository, stacks/ with the manifests of each kind, blueprint.py for the settings as code, the bots and the update path; docs/security.md adds the trust boundaries between them. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/README.md#how-the-blueprint-works
documentation_security_justification: docs/security.md says what users can and cannot expect: copying runs no code of the blueprint, blueprint.py never handles the value of a secret and changes only the settings of repository.toml, a new release reaches a repository only as a checked pull request, the dashboard shows only public data; and which risks remain. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/docs/security.md#what-you-can-expect
documentation_quick_start_justification: The README's Start a repository shows the six commands from copier copy to a repository with its settings applied, and what is left once per repository. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/README.md#start-a-repository
documentation_current_justification: Documentation changes in the same pull request as the behavior it describes, as the checklist of the pull request template asks; the notes of every release are the changelog entries of its pull requests, and the Links workflow checks every link on every change and every week. Known defects of the documentation are tracked and fixed as issues.
documentation_achievements_justification: The front page (README) shows and links the OpenSSF Best Practices badge, next to the OpenSSF Scorecard, REUSE and CI badges. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/README.md
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The documents are Markdown that markdownlint checks, including alternative text for every image (MD045); the dashboard is a static HTML page with a language, a semantic table with header cells and links with text. The blueprint has no other user interface.
internationalization_justification: The template, its documents and blueprint.py are in English only; the README exists in German as well.
sites_password_security_justification: The project's sites are on GitHub: the repository, issues, releases, discussions and GitHub Pages for the dashboard. The project stores no passwords of its own; GitHub meets this criterion, as its details say.
maintenance_or_update_justification: Only the latest release gets fixes, and the upgrade path is automatic: the blueprint bot of every repository runs copier update to each new release and opens a pull request, which merges once every check passes or shows its conflicts to the maintainer. A breaking change is a major version, whose notes say what to do. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/README.md#updates
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerability was reported or resolved in the last 12 months; the repository has no security advisory. SECURITY.md promises credit in the advisory and the release notes to every reporter who doesn't prefer anonymity. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SECURITY.md#what-happens-next
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md documents the process: private reporting through GitHub, acknowledgement within 7 days, a first assessment within 14 days, a fix of a confirmed vulnerability within 90 days at the latest, an update at least every 14 days when it takes longer, and disclosure in a GitHub security advisory and the release notes with credit for the reporter. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SECURITY.md#what-happens-next
coding_standards_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md names the style guides that contributions must follow: PEP 8 in the format of Ruff with the Ruff rules of pyproject.toml and strict mypy for Python, ShellCheck for shell scripts, actionlint and zizmor for workflows, markdownlint for Markdown and .editorconfig for every text file; and the same for every kind of project that the template creates. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#coding-standards
coding_standards_enforced_justification: scripts/check.sh runs ruff format --check, ruff check and mypy --strict, the Lint workflow actionlint, markdownlint, REUSE and the DCO check, and zizmor audits the workflows; all are required checks of every pull request. Exceptions are rare and marked in the code with their reason.
build_standard_variables_justification: The project produces no native binaries: the blueprint is a Copier template with Python scripts that run from source.
build_preserve_debug_justification: There is no compiled build: the blueprint is a Copier template with Python scripts that run from source.
build_non_recursive_justification: There is no build system that builds subdirectories: the blueprint is a Copier template with Python scripts that run from source.
build_repeatable_justification: No building occurs: the release is the tagged commit of the template and the Python scripts, which run from source.
installation_standard_variables_justific: There is no POSIX installation step that writes to a chosen location: Copier decides where the files go.
installation_development_quick_justifica: CONTRIBUTING.md shows how to set up everything to make and test changes: a virtual environment and pip install --require-hashes -r requirements-dev.txt, then bash scripts/check.sh runs every check of the CI. The dev container in .devcontainer/ sets it up in one step for VS Code and GitHub Codespaces, and git config core.hooksPath .githooks runs the checks before every push. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#checks
external_dependencies_justification: The dependencies are listed in requirements-dev.in and pinned with hashes in requirements-dev.txt; those of every kind of project in the manifests and lock files of stacks/. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/requirements-dev.txt
dependency_monitoring_justification: Renovate updates the dependencies, an update that fixes a vulnerability at once; OSV-Scanner checks every lock file on every pull request and every week and reports to code scanning, where the Findings workflow keeps every finding fixed or accepted with a reason; the dependency review blocks pull requests that bring in a dependency with a known vulnerability. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/.github/workflows/osv-scanner.yml
updateable_reused_components_justificati: Every dependency comes from a package manager, pinned in a lock file with hashes, and Renovate updates it; the repository holds no copy of third-party code.
interfaces_current_justification: Ruff's pyupgrade rules (UP) replace outdated Python constructs, pytest turns every warning, deprecations included, into an error (filterwarnings = error), and Renovate keeps actions and tools on current versions.
automated_integration_testing_justificat: The CI runs scripts/check.sh, the whole test suite with its coverage gate, on every push to main and on every pull request, and reports success or failure as required checks; the Variants workflow renders every kind of project and runs its own checks with its real tools. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci-python.yml
regression_tests_added50_justification: Of the 11 bugs fixed in the last six months, 5 brought a test in tests/ that fails without the fix, and 2 more are guarded by a required check that fails on the regression (zizmor for the pin of setup-php, REUSE for the license choice); the rest were fixes of the release workflows.
test_statement_coverage80_justification: scripts/check.sh runs pytest under coverage.py, a FLOSS tool, and fails below 100 % of the lines and branches of blueprint.py and dashboard.py (fail_under = 100 in pyproject.toml). https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/pyproject.toml
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md has the written policy: new functionality comes with tests in the automated test suite, in the same pull request, and every fix with a test that fails without it; a pull request without the tests it needs is not merged. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
implement_secure_design_justification: The repository and its releases apply least privilege, fail-safe defaults, complete mediation, separation of privilege, least common mechanism, economy of mechanism, open design and psychological acceptability, as the assurance case of SECURITY.md shows; docs/security.md shows the secure design of the software: no code runs when a repository is copied, blueprint.py never handles the value of a secret, every update is a pull request that passes the checks of each repository. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/docs/security.md
input_validation_justification: The answers of the Copier questions pass their validators (allowlists such as ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9]$ for names); blueprint.py reads every answer of GitHub strictly and stops on anything else, which coverage-guided fuzzing with Atheris checks. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/docs/security.md#trust-boundaries
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The software implements no cryptographic algorithm of its own; TLS comes from the GitHub CLI and Python's standard library, which verify certificates by default, and the signatures of releases from Sigstore.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: The blueprint stores no credentials. The secrets of a repository live in its GitHub environments, separate from every file, and are replaced with gh secret set without any change of code; blueprint.py only names the missing ones.
signed_releases_justification: Releases are immutable; GitHub signs an attestation that ties each tag to its commit and files, and the release workflow signs the build provenance of every file with Sigstore, without a long-lived key. SECURITY.md documents how users verify a release with gh release verify. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verify-a-release
version_tags_signed_justification: Every release tag since v0.6.0 is an annotated tag that the release workflow signs without a key with gitsign: Sigstore certifies the identity of the release workflow, and the release check verifies the signature and that identity after every release and every week. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/.github/sign-tag.sh https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/releases/tag/v0.6.0
small_tasks_justification: Small tasks for new or casual contributors carry the label good first issue, which CONTRIBUTING.md names and GitHub lists on the page Contribute: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/contribute
secure_2FA_justification: The only person with write access to the repository, its maintainer, signs in to GitHub with two-factor authentication (a passkey and an authenticator app), which GitHub also asks for again before sensitive settings. Everyone else changes the repository only through pull requests that he merges.
code_review_standards_justification: GOVERNANCE.md documents the code review: how a pull request is reviewed, what the review checks and what a pull request needs to be accepted: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#reviews
two_person_review_justification: The ruleset of main, which the settings bot applies, lets a change reach main only through a pull request, with no exception, not even for administrators: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SECURITY.md#trust-boundaries [osps_ac_03_01]
security_review_justification: SECURITY.md has the assurance case of the repository and its releases: the threat model, the trust boundaries, the secure design principles and how the OWASP Top 10 CI/CD security risks are countered, with CodeQL for the CWE Top 25. docs/security.md completes it for the blueprint itself: what it protects, its trust boundaries, its threats with countermeasures and tests, and the residual risks. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SECURITY.md#assurance-case https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/docs/security.md [assurance_case] [osps_sa_03_01]
assurance_case_justification: SECURITY.md has the assurance case of the repository and its releases: the threat model, the trust boundaries, the secure design principles and how the OWASP Top 10 CI/CD security risks are countered, with CodeQL for the CWE Top 25. docs/security.md completes it for the blueprint itself: what it protects, its trust boundaries, its threats with countermeasures and tests, and the residual risks. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SECURITY.md#assurance-case https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/docs/security.md
maintained_justification: Actively maintained; the blueprint serves the maintainer's repositories, and Dependabot, the release bot and the CI run continuously.
OSPS-AC-02.01_justification: GitHub gives a new collaborator no access until a maintainer invites them by hand, in an organization with the role that the invitation names, and the settings as code give no person any access: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#maintainers-and-access
OSPS-AC-03.01_justification: The ruleset of main, which the settings bot applies, lets a change reach main only through a pull request, with no exception, not even for administrators: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SECURITY.md#trust-boundaries
OSPS-AC-03.02_justification: The ruleset of main, which the settings bot applies, keeps everybody from deleting main or force-pushing it, with no exception: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SECURITY.md#trust-boundaries
OSPS-BR-01.01_justification: No workflow writes an untrusted value, such as the title of a pull request or the text of an issue, into a script: each one reaches it as an environment variable, and zizmor's audit of template injection checks every workflow: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/.github/workflows/zizmor.yml
OSPS-BR-03.01_justification: The channels of the project, the repository with its issues, discussions and releases on GitHub and the website on GitHub Pages, are served only over HTTPS: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint
OSPS-BR-03.02_justification: Releases are distributed over HTTPS, from GitHub, with an attestation of GitHub and the build provenance signed with Sigstore, which gh release verify checks: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verify-a-release
OSPS-BR-07.01_justification: GitHub's secret scanning with push protection, which the settings as code turn on, stops a known kind of secret before it lands, and Gitleaks scans every pull request and, every week, the whole history: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/.github/workflows/secret-scan.yml
OSPS-DO-02.01_justification: SUPPORT.md and the form for bugs say how to report a defect: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SUPPORT.md
OSPS-GV-02.01_justification: GitHub Issues and pull requests, and GitHub Discussions, open to everyone, for proposed changes and for problems of use: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/issues
OSPS-LE-02.01_justification: The source code is under the MIT-0 license, which the Open Source Initiative approves: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/LICENSE
OSPS-LE-02.02_justification: The released assets are under the MIT-0 license of the source code, which the Open Source Initiative approves: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/LICENSE
OSPS-LE-03.01_justification: The license is in the file LICENSE of the repository, and REUSE.toml gives the license of every file: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/LICENSE
OSPS-LE-03.02_justification: Every release contains the file LICENSE: the source code of its tag, which GitHub attaches to the release, holds it: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/LICENSE
OSPS-QA-01.01_justification: The repository is public at a static URL: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint
OSPS-QA-01.02_justification: Git records every change, who made it and when, and the history of main is public: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/commits/main
OSPS-QA-02.01_justification: pyproject.toml and requirements-dev.in list the direct dependencies, and requirements-dev.txt pins each with its hashes: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/requirements-dev.in
OSPS-QA-05.01_justification: Git holds the sources, from which every release builds what it ships: the step Binary files of scripts/check.sh, a required check, fails on a program, a library, compiled code or an archive in Git, whatever the name of its file: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/scripts/check.sh
OSPS-QA-05.02_justification: The step Binary files of scripts/check.sh, a required check, fails on every binary file in Git but pictures, videos, sounds, fonts, documents and the inputs of the fuzz tests, which a person can review: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/scripts/check.sh
OSPS-VM-02.01_justification: SECURITY.md names the security contact, the private vulnerability reporting of GitHub, which reaches the maintainers that GOVERNANCE.md lists: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability
OSPS-AC-04.01_justification: The token of a workflow may only read by default, a setting of the settings as code, and every workflow sets read-only or no permissions at its top: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/.github/repository.toml
OSPS-BR-02.01_justification: release-please gives every release a version of its own and a tag of the same name: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/releases
OSPS-BR-04.01_justification: Every release has its notes in CHANGELOG.md and in its GitHub release, with every change for users and every security fix: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
OSPS-BR-05.01_justification: Every dependency is installed with the standard tools of its ecosystem from a lock file, pinned by version and hash, every action by its commit hash and every image by its digest: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SECURITY.md#trust-boundaries
OSPS-BR-06.01_justification: GitHub signs an attestation of every release with the SHA-256 digest of each of its files, and the release workflow signs the build provenance of every file with Sigstore: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verify-a-release
OSPS-DO-06.01_justification: SECURITY.md describes how the project selects its dependencies, obtains them through their package managers from lock files that pin each by version and hash, and tracks them with Renovate, OSV-Scanner and the SBOMs of every release: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependencies
OSPS-GV-01.01_justification: GOVERNANCE.md lists the people with access to the repository, the releases and the security advisories: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#maintainers-and-access
OSPS-GV-01.02_justification: GOVERNANCE.md describes the roles maintainer, contributor, reporter and bots with their responsibilities: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities
OSPS-GV-03.02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states what an acceptable contribution needs: tests, the passing checks, the coding standards and a sign-off on every commit: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#requirements-for-changes
OSPS-LE-01.01_justification: Every commit carries a Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off, with which its author asserts the right to contribute it: the check DCO fails without one, and the settings as code require it for commits made on github.com: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#requirements-for-changes
OSPS-QA-03.01_justification: The ruleset of main lets a pull request merge only once every required check of the settings as code has passed on the latest main, with no exception: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/.github/repository.toml
OSPS-QA-06.01_justification: A required check runs scripts/check.sh with the test suite on every pull request before it can merge: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/scripts/check.sh
OSPS-SA-01.01_justification: The README explains the high-level design: copier.yml with the questions, template/ with the files whose names carry their conditions, the workflows of this repository as the templates of every repository, stacks/ with the manifests of each kind, blueprint.py for the settings as code, the bots and the update path; docs/security.md adds the trust boundaries between them. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/README.md#how-the-blueprint-works [documentation_architecture]
OSPS-SA-02.01_justification: The README documents the questions of the template, the files and workflows a repository gets, the settings as code of blueprint.py and the updates: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint#readme [documentation_interface]
OSPS-SA-03.01_justification: SECURITY.md has the assurance case of the repository and its releases: the threat model, the trust boundaries, the secure design principles and how the OWASP Top 10 CI/CD security risks are countered, with CodeQL for the CWE Top 25. docs/security.md completes it for the blueprint itself: what it protects, its trust boundaries, its threats with countermeasures and tests, and the residual risks. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SECURITY.md#assurance-case https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/docs/security.md [assurance_case]
OSPS-VM-01.01_justification: SECURITY.md has the policy of coordinated disclosure with its times: an acknowledgement within 7 days, a first assessment within 14 days, a fix within 90 days at the latest, and the disclosure with the fixed release: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SECURITY.md#what-happens-next
OSPS-VM-03.01_justification: The private vulnerability reporting of GitHub, which SECURITY.md names: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/security/advisories/new
OSPS-VM-04.01_justification: A fixed vulnerability is published in a GitHub security advisory and in the release notes, as SECURITY.md says: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SECURITY.md#what-happens-next
OSPS-AC-04.02_justification: Every workflow starts with read-only or no permissions, and each job gets only those that it needs; zizmor audits the permissions of every workflow: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/.github/workflows/zizmor.yml
OSPS-BR-02.02_justification: Every file of a release is attached to the immutable release of its tag, which the attestation of GitHub ties to it, and its SBOMs carry the version of the release: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verify-a-release
OSPS-BR-07.02_justification: SECURITY.md has the policy for secrets and credentials: how they are stored, in the environments of GitHub and never in Git, who can use them and how, and when and how they are replaced: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SECURITY.md#secrets-and-credentials
OSPS-DO-03.01_justification: SECURITY.md shows how to verify the integrity and the authenticity of a release with gh release verify: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verify-a-release
OSPS-DO-03.02_justification: The certificate of Sigstore names the release workflow of the repository as the author of a release, and SECURITY.md shows how to check it: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verify-a-release
OSPS-DO-04.01_justification: SECURITY.md: security fixes are provided for the latest release: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
OSPS-DO-05.01_justification: SECURITY.md: only the latest release gets security fixes, so a release gets none once the next one is published: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
OSPS-GV-04.01_justification: GOVERNANCE.md has the policy: before a person gets escalated permissions, such as the right to merge, the secrets or the security advisories, the maintainers review their contributions, their identity, their two-factor authentication and the signatures of their commits: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#maintainers-and-access
OSPS-QA-02.02_justification: Every release carries SBOMs of what it ships, as SPDX and as CycloneDX: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verify-a-release
OSPS-QA-06.02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md says how to run the tests, with bash scripts/check.sh and before every push with the hook, and the CI runs them on every pull request: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#checks
OSPS-QA-06.03_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md has the policy: changes need tests, and the checks of scripts/check.sh pass: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#requirements-for-changes
OSPS-QA-07.01_justification: The ruleset of main, which the settings bot applies, lets a change reach main only through a pull request, with no exception, not even for administrators: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SECURITY.md#trust-boundaries [osps_ac_03_01] [two_person_review]
OSPS-SA-03.02_justification: SECURITY.md has the assurance case of the repository and its releases: the threat model, the trust boundaries, the secure design principles and how the OWASP Top 10 CI/CD security risks are countered, with CodeQL for the CWE Top 25. docs/security.md completes it for the blueprint itself: what it protects, its trust boundaries, its threats with countermeasures and tests, and the residual risks. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SECURITY.md#assurance-case https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/docs/security.md [assurance_case]
OSPS-VM-04.02_justification: When the project accepts an advisory in osv-scanner.toml, with its reason, the release carries an OpenVEX document that tells scanners that the advisory doesn't affect it: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verify-a-release
OSPS-VM-05.01_justification: Renovate updates the dependencies, an update that fixes a vulnerability at once; OSV-Scanner checks every lock file on every pull request and every week and reports to code scanning, where the Findings workflow keeps every finding fixed or accepted with a reason; the dependency review blocks pull requests that bring in a dependency with a known vulnerability. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/.github/workflows/osv-scanner.yml [dependency_monitoring]
OSPS-VM-05.02_justification: Renovate updates the dependencies, an update that fixes a vulnerability at once; OSV-Scanner checks every lock file on every pull request and every week and reports to code scanning, where the Findings workflow keeps every finding fixed or accepted with a reason; the dependency review blocks pull requests that bring in a dependency with a known vulnerability. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/.github/workflows/osv-scanner.yml [dependency_monitoring]
OSPS-VM-05.03_justification: Renovate updates the dependencies, an update that fixes a vulnerability at once; OSV-Scanner checks every lock file on every pull request and every week and reports to code scanning, where the Findings workflow keeps every finding fixed or accepted with a reason; the dependency review blocks pull requests that bring in a dependency with a known vulnerability. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/.github/workflows/osv-scanner.yml [dependency_monitoring]
OSPS-VM-06.01_justification: SECURITY.md sets the threshold: a new alert of CodeQL of high or critical severity, or a new error, stops the merge, and so does every new alert of zizmor, and the Findings workflow fails while a finding is open that isn't accepted with its reason: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SECURITY.md#findings-of-code-scanning
OSPS-VM-06.02_justification: CodeQL analyzes every pull request as a required check, and the ruleset of main stops the merge of one that adds an alert of high or critical severity; a finding is accepted only with its reason in .github/findings.toml: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/.github/findings.toml
OSPS-BR-01.03_justification: The workflows of a pull request run with a read-only token and without secrets, every secret is in an environment that only main may use, and the workflows of outside contributors wait for the maintainer's approval: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/SECURITY.md#trust-boundaries
OSPS-DO-07.01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md shows how to set up everything to make and test changes: a virtual environment and pip install --require-hashes -r requirements-dev.txt, then bash scripts/check.sh runs every check of the CI. The dev container in .devcontainer/ sets it up in one step for VS Code and GitHub Codespaces, and git config core.hooksPath .githooks runs the checks before every push. https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#checks [installation_development_quick]
OSPS-BR-01.04_justification: The inputs of a workflow, also those of collaborators, reach its scripts only as environment variables, never in the text of a script, which zizmor's audit of template injection checks: https://github.com/Dennis-Otto/repo-blueprint/blob/main/.github/workflows/zizmor.yml
